excerpt: You rewrote your mining code to keep more of your gold, and the largest mine is working again.
paras: You rewrote your mining code to keep more of your gold, and the largest mine is working again. On the last measure, nine in ten of your children could not read by the end of primary school. Let the gold buy the schools, the power and the water that the next generation needs.

Your partners have stayed. In March 2026 the World Bank approved $150 million to keep essential services open, after $219.8 million in 2025 for the roads that connect your regions. Your humanitarian partners have set out a plan of $551 million for 2026. At home, your Government says a fund backed by your mines could unlock up to $800 million for infrastructure.

The work ahead is plain, and it is worth saying plainly. Only two in every hundred of you cook with clean fuel, and about half have electricity. Ninety-three in every hundred of your city dwellers live in slums. At the last count, in 2012, ninety in every hundred of your children reached the end of primary school unable to read a simple text. Clean energy sets your Coverage today, at 2 out of 100, with shelter and reading close behind. Each of them is within your reach.

Now imagine that same resolve turned toward every home in the country. Picture Perfect Mali: a morning when every family cooks with clean fuel and sits down to a full table; when every tap runs clean and every home has a safe toilet; when every child walks to a school where a teacher is waiting, and reads with ease by the age of ten; when every mother lives within reach of a clinic with the lights on, and every young person finds work that pays. And no Malian falls below a decent life, because the nation has decided that none will.
quote: Gold leaves the ground once. Let it build schools that teach every child, every year.
